name: Logistics
title: Shipment exception recovery desk
summary: Coordinate carrier evidence, dock capacity, and customer commitments for dispatcher-approved shipment recovery.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A third-party logistics operator manages delayed inbound loads to a distribution center. Carrier position feeds, driver messages, dock appointments, and customer delivery windows disagree. Dispatchers need feasible recovery options before a delay propagates into missed appointments and avoidable detention.
problem: Position estimates do not establish arrival, and driver messages cannot authorize a new commercial commitment. Rebooking one dock slot may strand another load. An agent workflow must reconcile operational constraints without interfering with driver safety or carrier control.
whyAgents: Tracking, appointment, customer-commitment, and recovery specialists investigate separate systems. A scheduling service evaluates feasible windows while agents explain uncertainty and coordinate a dispatcher-owned exception case.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Measure actionable recovery preparation and confirmed appointment outcomes. Delivery performance also depends on traffic, carrier execution, and facility operations, so improvements must be evaluated against comparable lanes rather than assumed.

agents.name: Tracking investigator
agents.responsibility: Compare carrier scans, last-known position, and estimated arrival freshness.
agents.boundary: Cannot direct vehicle movement or treat predictions as confirmed scans.

agents.name: Dock coordinator
agents.responsibility: Retrieve appointments, unloading capacity, and site restrictions.
agents.boundary: Cannot reserve or cancel slots without dispatcher approval.

agents.name: Commitment analyst
agents.responsibility: Find contractual delivery windows and approved escalation contacts.
agents.boundary: Cannot waive service terms or promise compensation.

agents.name: Recovery planner
agents.responsibility: Draft reroute, rebook, or hold options with dependencies and costs.
agents.boundary: Cannot assign unsafe driving schedules or tender loads autonomously.

systems.name: Transportation management system
systems.role: Owns loads, carrier assignments, commercial terms, and approved transport changes.

systems.name: Carrier visibility platform
systems.role: Supplies timestamped events and estimates with source-specific confidence and freshness.

systems.name: Dock and customer operations systems
systems.role: Expose capacity and delivery commitments while retaining local booking authority.

flow.title: Capture delay signal
flow.description: Deduplicate carrier events and attach load, leg, event time, and expected customer window.

flow.title: Check tracking quality
flow.description: Classify observations as confirmed scans, carrier estimates, or stale positions before calculating available recovery time.

flow.title: Gather constraints
flow.description: Read dock capacity, site restrictions, order commitments, and permitted carrier options from authoritative systems.

flow.title: Evaluate options
flow.description: Run route and appointment feasibility checks; show assumptions about arrival and unloading duration explicitly.

flow.title: Obtain dispatcher decision
flow.description: Present costs, affected parties, and unresolved conditions; communication drafts stay pending until the dispatcher approves them.

flow.title: Commit coordinated changes
flow.description: Reserve the selected appointment, submit approved transport changes, and reconcile each acknowledgement before announcing a confirmed recovery.

    participant O as "Case orchestrator"

O->>S: Read delayed load state
    O->>H: Propose dock rebooking

diagrams.caption: The position feed reports an impossible jump. The workflow records unresolved work and resumes only after the source state and reviewer authority are checked.

failures.scenario: The position feed reports an impossible jump.
failures.detection: Speed and event-order checks conflict with previous trusted scans.
failures.recovery: Discard the suspect estimate, retain the last confirmed event, and request carrier verification.

failures.scenario: Dock rebooking succeeds but carrier acceptance fails.
failures.detection: The workflow has a booking receipt without a corresponding carrier acknowledgement.
failures.recovery: Hold the recovery as partial and release or retain the slot according to the dispatcher's approved compensation policy.

controls: Keep driver safety and legal driving constraints in validated planning services and human dispatch procedures.
Distinguish estimated arrival from carrier-confirmed arrival in every output.
Bind changes to load, leg, carrier, appointment, and source revision.
Restrict customer contract retrieval by account assignment and operating region.
Track appointment reservations with expiry and compensating release actions.

metrics.name: Exception preparation time
metrics.definition: Time from reliable delay signal to dispatcher-reviewable recovery options.

metrics.name: Arrival evidence freshness
metrics.definition: Age of the latest trusted tracking event when a recovery decision is presented.

metrics.name: Recovery acknowledgement rate
metrics.definition: Approved plans with every required carrier and facility receipt divided by approved plans.

metrics.name: Reservation leakage
metrics.definition: Expired or abandoned dock reservations remaining active beyond their release deadline.

tradeoffs.benefit: Provides a useful dispatch picture before windows close.
tradeoffs.cost: Needs reconciliation of different source timestamps.
Temporary reservations can reduce utilization if not released promptly.

tradeoffs.benefit: Prevents false claims that recovery is complete.
tradeoffs.cost: Adds workflow states and dispatcher follow-up work.

rollout.acceptance: Dispatchers verify estimate labeling, route constraints, and contract-window interpretation against known outcomes.
One lane group assesses plan usability and tracking freshness without booking changes.
Selected facilities enable changes after partial-acknowledgement and reservation-release drills succeed.
